SM22L-A1.free_elimination: No clean free strike. 36 = k^2 (det k^2-36=0) is readable as a shortcut value, but it is also the key, so the shortcut 'c is 36 because 36 appears' would pick the key without the decision (k=6 must give infinitely many solutions => c/6=6). -12 is the mirrored case (k=-6 coincident, k=6 inconsistent). 18 and 24 need a check to strike (both make both k values inconsistent).
SM22L-A1.note: det=k^2-36 -> k=+/-6. For exactly one (negative) no-solution value, k=6 must be coincident: 2x+y=6 and 2x+y=c/6 -> c=36. Check k=-6: -2x+y=2 vs -2x+y=-6, no solution. Mild concern: key equals k^2, a number a guesser could associate with the stem.

SM22L-A2.free_elimination: Adjacency: two adjacent pairs (7,8) and (11,12), so the classic lone-pair tell is weakened but the set is clearly two boundary pairs. 'Smallest' with a monotone condition points to the lower pair; a test-wise student would strike 11 and 12 as upper-boundary values (12 is the max of 7<k<=12). Then 7 vs 8 is the strict-inequality decision.
SM22L-A2.note: 8+k>5x -> x<(8+k)/5; need 3<(8+k)/5<=4 -> 7<k<=12; smallest integer 8. Structure of option set (lower pair vs upper pair) gives away half the set to a student who reads 'smallest'.

SM22L-A3.free_elimination: Direction: shifting left by 6 equals shifting down by 4 means the line falls as x increases (negative slope). A falling line through (3,7) crosses y=0 to the right of x=3, so -15/2 and -5/3 are struck with only the sign reasoning. Remaining 23/3 vs 27/2 needs |m| = 2/3 vs 3/2 (rise/run inversion).
SM22L-A3.note: f(x+6)=f(x)-4 -> 6m=-4 -> m=-2/3; 0=7-2/3(x-3) -> x=27/2. Distractors map to m=2/3, 3/2, -3/2. Sign kill leaves a 50/50 on reciprocal slope.

SM22L-A4.free_elimination: None clean. Shop B's own intercept is 30 (slope 1.5 through (50,105)); options 45 = 30+15, 60, 75 are not readable by a free heuristic. Plugging options back requires the slope work.
SM22L-A4.note: A(30)=90, A(70)=150 -> slope 1.5 -> fee 90-45=45. The shift-by-20 is the decision; once seen it is routine.

SM22L-A5.free_elimination: None free. 103 exceeds the LP bound (1320/13 = 101.5) and 101 is the floor of the LP optimum, but both require computing the vertex. No range bound printed.
SM22L-A5.note: Integer optimum (L,S)=(6,9): 72 roses? 7*6+3*9=69<=72, 5*6+4*9=66<=66, profit 99. LP vertex (90/13,102/13) gives 101.5 -> 101 distractor is the 'round the corner' error. Enumeration confirms 99 is max (next 98). Integer linear programming is at the edge of SAT Algebra scope (linear inequalities in two variables) - atypical but inside the listed skill.

SM22L-A6.free_elimination: Two adjacent pairs (4,5) and (12,13). 'Greatest' points at the upper element of a pair; a test-wise student picks between 12/13 or prefers larger values. Not a lone-pair tell, but the paired structure signals the boundary decision. Weak: 4/5 strike only after finding c<=13.
SM22L-A6.note: Overlap needs 3x-7<c-2x -> x<(c+7)/5; no x>=4 iff (c+7)/5<=4 -> c<=13. At c=13 strict inequalities exclude x=4. Key decision: boundary inclusion (13 vs 12). Desmos with slider for c reaches it quickly (insight partially bypassable visually, but boundary still needs reasoning).

SM22L-A7.free_elimination: None clean. 7 is the shortcut 'match the constant 7' ; 16 = 3*3+7 sign error; 3 is the k value. Each wrong option is a plausible step value; nothing strikeable without the k=3 decision.
SM22L-A7.note: (2k-6)x = c+3k-7. Only k=3 can fail; requires c+9-7=0 -> c=-2. Decision: realise only the degenerate k matters.

SM22L-B1.free_elimination: 3 is the B-A=-4 sign pair (A taller by 4). Not free without the line. No range bound kill: all four times keep both candles burning? A burns out at 10 h, so all options valid on that ground.
SM22L-B1.note: B(t)=30-2t, A(t)=40-4t; B-A=2t-10=4 -> t=7. Desmos intersection of B and A+4 bypasses nothing hard; there is no real decision beyond building B's equation.

SM22L-B2.free_elimination: Monotonicity: h=f-g rises from -5 at x=2 to 7 at x=6; target h=-4 lies between, just above -5, so x is in (2,6) and close to 2. Strikes 1/3 (left of 2) for free and makes 5 implausible (near where h is large). 11/3 (root of h) and 5 (h=+4, sign flip) are the remaining traps.
SM22L-B2.note: h(x)=3x-11; h=-4 -> x=7/3. Insight (work with f-g) is the only decision and is standard.

SM22L-B3.free_elimination: Plugging back is trivially quick: A=B+20 from the first condition, then test each option (70,50 -> 80 vs 40 works). One or two plugs finish it.
SM22L-B3.note: A-10=B+10, A+10=2(B-10) -> B=50, A=70. Standard textbook system; no decision point. 50 (B) offered as distractor.

SM22L-B4.free_elimination: Range bound: 16/1.2 = 13.3 is the max with no food at all, and food is required, so 13 is struck free (it is the shortcut skipping the food constraint).
SM22L-B4.note: Minimum food 2w: 1.2w+1.6w<=16 -> w<=5.71 -> 5. 10 = f>=w/2 reversal, 8 = f>=w.

SM22L-B5.free_elimination: 33 = time from 9:00 (stem explicitly asks after gate opens) - struck by reading the reference point; it is also 18+15, closed under adding the 15-minute offset. 8 = 120/15 ignores the 150 joiners pre-opening.
SM22L-B5.note: 270 at 9:15, net -15/min -> 18 min. Routine rate problem.

SM22L-B6.free_elimination: 5/2 is x/y (intermediate shortcut value) and 7/2 = x/y+1 (numerator over y); option set is closed under the intermediate operations, so a student who finds x/y=5/2 can see two options built from it. Not a free strike without the first step.

SM22L-B7.free_elimination: 22 = 9+13 and 40 = 27+13 are sums of the printed constants (option set built from the RHS values); a student guessing 'some combination of 9 and 13' cannot separate them for free. No strike.
SM22L-B7.note: 3*eq1 - eq2 = x+8y-7z -> 27-13=14. Also bypassable: set z=0 and solve the 2x2 (x+3y=9, 2x+y=13 -> y=1, x=6) -> 6+8=14. Three unknowns is outside 'systems of two linear equations in two variables'; borderline off-blueprint.
